description: How short-form video rewrote advertising: TikTok rose from nothing to a dominant ad engine while incumbents (YouTube, Facebook/Meta, Snapchat) fought to adapt. This year-by-year ad-revenue race (2007–2026) shows TikTok’s meteoric climb after 2016, YouTube’s steady strength, Meta’s massive legacy ad base, and Snapchat’s slower, steady growth—driven by pandemic adoption, product pivots (Reels/Shorts), and changing creative formats.
youtube_description: The Short-Form Takeover — Watch how short-form video remade the ad world. TikTok went from near-zero ad dollars to a multi‑billion advertising engine in under a decade while legacy platforms scrambled to clone the format (Reels, Shorts) and protect their ad bases. This visualization uses company-reported ad revenues (and widely cited ByteDance estimates) year-by-year from 2007–2026 to tell the story of platform power shifting to short, swipeable content.
